articleTitle: Application of motion compensation to video processing in the TV studio
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Video Processing in the TV Studio
abstract: Recent advances in VLSI technology and algorithm development are enabling motion estimation and compensation techniques to be applied to many processes in the TV studio. The range of possible applications is very wide and each places particular demands on the motion estimator. The paper reviews some of the attributes of motion estimators and compares them with the requirements of various processes, drawing on experiences gained in recent work. Processes that are amenable to motion compensation that are considered include standards conversion, slow-motion and film motion improvement (each involving the interpolation of new images using motion compensation), film unsteadiness correction, noise reduction, film dirt concealment and bandwidth reduction for HDTV.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Colorimetric noise performance of component colour video signals
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Video Processing in the TV Studio
abstract: Objective and subjective impairments in a displayed colour picture can be evaluated accurately by analysing the component colour video signals. Objective noise performance of component colour video signals in a TV monitor is investigated. This analysis takes in to account the effect of nonlinearity of the display tube. The impairment in the displayed picture is a function of the magnitude and spectra of the input noise. Two commonly occurring noise spectra are considered. They are triangular (deemphasised), and white noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Video Processing in the TV Studio
abstract: Discusses the operation of digital video effects (DVE) equipment. The first DVE equipment was developed from the digital component frame synchroniser. A digital filter can help to solve some of the processing problems, in that it can function as a low pass filter which removes the HF energy from the picture signal, before the size of the picture is reduced, thus removing the alias components from the final output. It can also be set up to delay the signal by a controlled amount, resulting in displacement of the picture in increment smaller than one pixel.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Video Processing in the TV Studio
abstract: Identifies the sources and examines the results of picture processing in the post production area of television where no studio floor as such need exist. In terms of image manipulation, post production can be divided into: editing, matting, composting; colour grading, matching; resizing, reshaping images, digital video effects; motion effects; and 3D painting. All of the above processes are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Where have we come from, and where are we going? (digital TV studio)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Video Processing in the TV Studio
abstract: Examines the route to the development of the all digital TV studio. The earliest digital video equipment were experimental and prototype ADCs. This was followed by a video tape time-base corrector. 1976 saw the introduction of frame store synchronizers based on RAM, and digital video effects in the form of position manipulation and reduced picture size. As a result of current studies into Improved (IDTV), High (HDTV) and Enhanced (EDTV) systems, intermediate standards may be needed due to the frequency brickwall inherent with the current 601 specification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real time interactive object creation and manipulation-DME 9000
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Video Processing in the TV Studio
abstract: The goal of the research at Sony was to provide a means for easy manipulation of texture mapped surfaces and to make texture mapping useful in such applications as free form surface design and facial animation. This research has produced a fast texture mapping algorithm applicable to the generation of arbitrary shapes. The algorithm determines a linear approximation of the mapping function over small areas which form the curved surfaces and is known as extended locally linear approximation (ELLA). A digital video effects unit, the DME 9000, has been developed to implement ELLA. The DME 9000 consists of a controller and a processor. The controller is composed of a specially designed control panel. The processor consists of an address generator and a video signal processor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Video Processing in the TV Studio
abstract: A new serial digital interface is being proposed to handle both 4:2:2 digital component video and 4fsc digital composite video. It is a 10 bit system that also allows for possible expansion of the current 8 bit digital video standard, CCIR-601. Sony is manufacturing this serial digital IC with a complete range of coprocessors. The use of scrambled nonreturn to zero inverted has made it possible to implement a complete serialiser and deserialiser each on a single VLSI chip.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
